title: Canonical completed refinement natural transformation

from.place: Proof step 8, C_u before evaluating at K.

statement: Let d be an adic coefficient datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], with completed coefficient derived categories and canonical ordinary operations [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Let f:X→Y be quasi-compact, c1,c2 compactifications [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification] and u:c1→c2 a proper refinement [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Use the section-normalized open extension functors J_j and adjunctions [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], and put F_c=J_j followed by Rp_*. Define the natural transformation F_c2→F_c1 by inverse identity unitor, whiskering of J_j2 applied to the inverse proper identity comparison followed by the proper/open mate gamma for the square (j1,1_X,u,j2) [lem-cbc-proper-open-clopen-projector], the functor associator, the proper direct-image composition comparison, and the equality u;p2=p1. The identity and composition comparisons are the specified canonical ones [lem-weil-pbc-completed-ordinary-comparisons]. All factors are specified natural transformations. Its component is the canonical map C_u in blueprint proof step 8. No invertibility of C_u, completeness of input, or refinement functoriality is asserted by this definition.

source.place: Tags 0F7B and 0F7C; canonical proper/open refinement comparison C_u, blueprint thm-cbc-complete-proetale proof step 8.

proof.text: Construct the displayed composite of natural transformations. The intermediate functors match after the explicit left unitor and associator. Properness of u and of the compactification projections supplies the proper/open mate; quasi-compactness of each open immersion follows from quasi-compactness of f. Naturality is inherited by composition and whiskering. The two categorical coherence maps have identity components, so functor map_id and category unit laws recover the original component formula. This construction involves no unproved existence choice.

mathlib_searches.results: Eight general condensed and affine-transition results; no canonical proper/open refinement construction.
Eleven coherence lemmas for bicategories, monoidal categories and Join; none constructs the geometric comparison. The standard functor coherence maps are used explicitly.
